concept at 1:35:48,
drop_first=True removes the very first column when converting words into numbers.
The Simple Example is if you have a column for Traffic Lights with three colors: 
Red, Yellow, and Green.Normally,

 the computer creates 3 new columns:
Column 1: Red (1 if red, 0 if not)
Column 2: Yellow (1 if yellow, 0 if not)
Column 3: Green (1 if green, 0 if not)

What drop_first=True Does It deletes the Green column (the first one alphabetically).

You are left with just two columns: Red and Yellow.
The computer can still easily figure out the color:
If Red is 1, it is Red.
If Yellow is 1, it is Yellow.
If both are 0, it must be Green.

Status: Research concept (not an existing or validated model).

Goal

AyamGNN is designed for:

Knowledge graphs

Power-grid analysis

Financial transaction networks

Multi-agent systems

Robotics


Core Architecture

Input Graph
      │
Node Encoder
      │
Edge Encoder
      │
Adaptive Graph Attention
      │
Dynamic Message Passing
      │
Hierarchical Graph Pooling
      │
Global Memory Layer
      │
Prediction Head

Layer Update

For node \(i\):

\[
h_i^{(l+1)}
=
\sigma\!\left(
W_1h_i^{(l)}
+
\sum_{j\in\mathcal N(i)}
\alpha_{ij}W_2h_j^{(l)}
+
M^{(l)}
\right)
\]

where:

\(h_i^{(l)}\) = node embedding

\(\alpha_{ij}\) = learned attention weight

\(M^{(l)}\) = global graph memory

\(W_1, W_2\) = trainable matrices

Adaptive memory that stores long-range graph information.

Temporal graph updates for evolving networks.
